title: Adaptive burst smoothing and quota-enforcement failover
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: The current quota/rate-limiter struggles with short-duration bursts and has a single-path dependency on the centralized token refill service. Recent incidents showed both unfairness across customers during bursts and a catastrophic failure mode when the refill pipeline experienced backpressure. Goal: Implement an adaptive burst-smoothing layer, hierarchical fairness at customer+route granularity, and a robust degraded-mode failover that preserves SLOs and reduces cascading outages. Deliverables include algorithm design, Redis-backed state with local fallback, circuit-breaker thresholds, tests, dashboards, and a staged rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: Burst smoothing reduces 95th and 99th percentile request rejections during short bursts by >= 40% for synthetic burst tests
Quota enforcement latency (limiter decision path) stays under 100ms P99 in normal mode and under 250ms P99 in degraded mode
Fairness rules prevent any single customer from consuming > 60% of aggregate burst tokens within a 10s window
Limiter primary path availability >= 99.95% and degraded-mode availability >= 99.99% during simulated central-refill outages
Automated rollback trigger in console when rejected rate or latency exceeds safe thresholds during rollout
decision_log: 2025-02-19: Chose hybrid token-bucket + adaptive smoothing instead of pure leaky-bucket to keep per-request latency low while providing burst absorbtion.
2025-02-22: Use Redis primary for cross-region shared state with multi-AZ read replicas; local in-memory sliding window as fallback to preserve safety during Redis partitions.
2025-02-25: Implement hierarchical fairness: per-customer quota + per-route reserve. Reason: prevents noisy neighbors while keeping route-level SLOs intact.
2025-03-01: Degraded mode will employ probabilistic accept sampling (p=0.7 default) plus strict per-customer hard caps. Rationale: graceful degradation with configurable quality-cost tradeoff.
2025-03-03: Circuit breaker thresholds: open when limiter decision latency > 300ms for 30s and error rate > 5% across instances; half-open with canary traffic at 1%.
Trade-offs: Redis provides strong shared counters but increases surface area; local fallback favors availability at cost of stricter limits and potential false rejections.
Security note: quota enforcement logs will avoid storing PII; KMS keys required for any audit export. Security review requested.
work_updates: 2025-02-20: Spike implementation complete. Prototype smoothing algorithm (exponential dampening) evaluated against synthetic bursts. PR 1197 contains benchmarks.
2025-02-24: Integration test harness added to infra-ci to inject Redis latency and verify degraded-mode behavior. Observed degraded-mode decision latency median 120ms.
2025-02-27: Initial fairness policy config landed; cgroups-style weight enforcement implemented. Added e2e test that simulates 50 clients with Zipf distribution.
2025-03-02: PR 1213 submitted for Redis replication changes; initial security review comments addressed (audit logging removed for sensitive headers).
2025-03-04: Began canary rollout plan in us-east-1; canary job creates synthetic traffic to validate SLOs before expanding to more regions. Temporary metric alerts created in console.
Blocking: Waiting on PM-421 for final SLO thresholds and customer opt-in policy for probabilistic degradation.
review_feedback: PM (Lena Ortiz) 2025-02-21: Confirm that 'probabilistic accept' has explicit customer opt-out and clear UX messaging. Link to UX doc requested.
Design (Omar Ruiz) 2025-02-26: Dashboard mockups look good; request a summary view for affected tenants during degraded-mode with suggested remediation actions.
SRE (Priya Shah) 2025-02-28: Ensure circuit-breaker opens fast enough to protect downstream services; prefer conservative defaults and strong observability on fallback path.
Security (Anika Rao) 2025-03-01: Approve local fallback that stores only aggregate counters; forbid storage of full request payloads in limiter logs. Require KMS for exported audit blobs.
monitoring_playbook: Dashboards: 'Limiter Decisions' (per-region), 'Burst Absorbtion' (95/99p), 'Degraded Mode Activation' (count) and 'Fairness Violations' (tenant list). Runbook: runbooks/internal/limiter-failover.md (link: https://confluence.redwood.ai/runbooks/limiter-failover). Pager: on-call SRE to triage; immediate action is to toggle route to slower but stable variant or enable global degraded-mode if >3 regions report high limiter latency.
testing_plan: Unit tests for smoothing algorithm and fairness enforcement rules
Load tests: simulate 10k req/s with bursts up to 30k/s across 5 regions; verify metrics and SLOs
Chaos test: inject 200-500ms Redis latency and simulate master failover; validate local fallback correctness
Canary rollout with synthetic tenants and progressive increase in traffic (1% -> 10% -> 50%)
Post-deploy regression: run historical traffic replay for two busiest customers and compare acceptance/reject curves
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Feature-flagged code to runtime with no traffic (merge to main behind flag)
Stage 1: Internal canary in us-east-1 with synthetic traffic (1-2 days)
Stage 2: Broader canary covering 5% of production traffic and 2 geographic regions (3 days)
Stage 3: Gradual region-by-region ramp with automated health gates; abort on SLO regressions
Stage 4: Full global rollout and monitor for 7 days; finalize config and remove feature flag
notes: Related incident: incident-2024-11-rate-limiter-outage (postmortem: https://confluence.redwood.ai/incidents/2024-11-rate-limiter). That postmortem motivated local fallback and stricter fairness. PM must confirm billing/metrics semantics during degraded-mode (we may need special billing flags). Also coordinate with Legal for customers in regulated regions before enabling probabilistic accept by default.
